input: digits is a nonempty Array of decimal digits 0 through 9 with length n <= 4294967294. It represents a nonnegative integer most-significant digit first, with no leading zero except the single-digit representation [0]. String inputs, when present, are primitive strings, not boxed strings. Integer values are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays, not sparse arrays, proxies, subclasses or accessor-backed collections. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Allocation and runtime resource limits still require qualification; this declared domain is not a capacity or completion guarantee.
return: A fresh digit Array representing the input integer plus one, in canonical most-significant-first form. Its length is n or n + 1; no integer conversion or fixed-width truncation is performed.
mutation_aliasing: All inputs, their ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. Carry propagation changes only a fresh shallow copy. The returned sequence does not alias digits, including when no carry propagates. The all-nine branch allocates a second new sequence with leading 1; the discarded working copy is not returned or externally visible.
numeric: Only digits, indices and a single-digit increment are used. A changed digit stays in [0, 9]; there is no conversion of the whole represented value to Number or int. The n + 1 output-length bound fits a JavaScript Array.
complexity: O(n) worst-case time, including the initial copy and the all-nine concatenation. Retained output is O(n); auxiliary working storage is O(n) in the all-nine branch while concatenation creates the final output. No constant-extra-space or in-place-input claim is made.

There are no custom helper definitions, imports, generated implementations or hidden source expansion. Built-in operations are not free: their allocations and work are included in the stated runtime/storage costs.
